bull_case: Cheap repurchases plus steady FCF can compound per-share value even with only mid-single-digit revenue growth.
bear_case: If checkout economics deteriorate, buybacks alone cannot offset a shrinking earnings base.
thesis: PayPal has excellent FCF/share quality but a less compelling organic reinvestment runway. Its value creation currently comes more from harvesting a mature network and repurchasing discounted stock than from deploying large amounts of capital into high-return new growth.

evidence.claim: FY2025 owner-style FCF proxy was about $4.562B.
H1 2026 owner-style FCF proxy was about $2.093B.
Shares outstanding fell from about 920.7M in late Jan 2026 to 855.5M by July 22.

counterevidence: Branded checkout competition remains intense and active-account growth is essentially flat, limiting evidence of a widening moat.
falsifiers: If transaction-margin dollars contract persistently, branded checkout resumes material share loss, or buybacks stop creating FCF/share growth, the thesis weakens.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Strong FCF and improving per-share economics do not support a structural collapse in incremental returns.
The company is materially reducing shares outstanding, not persistently diluting owners.

key_kpis.name: owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: sustained growth despite modest revenue growth

next_checks: Branded checkout growth, Venmo revenue, transaction-margin dollars, active accounts, TPV, repurchases, diluted shares

subscores.rationale: PayPal converts modest revenue growth into substantial FCF and rising per-share economics through cost discipline and buybacks.
Internal high-return reinvestment absorption is modest; a large portion of excess capital is returned via repurchases rather than deployed into new high-ROIC growth.
Owner-style FCF is strong and the share count is shrinking rapidly, directly increasing FCF/share.

uncertainties.rationale: Payments competition and transformation execution remain the primary uncertainty.
